paragraphs: Founded in 1955, we are one of the leading designers and manufacturers of products sold to consumers, primarily through retail channels, in the tools, outdoor living and celebrations market categories as well as a wide array of highly specialized building products that primarily serve customers in the residential and non-residential construction markets, including ceiling suspension systems and light gauge metal framing products, respectively, through our unconsolidated joint ventures, WAVE and ClarkDietrich, as well as wholly-owned and consolidated operations that produce pressurized containment solutions for heating, cooking and cooling applications, among others. Our business strategy is rooted in our people first culture that values our relationships across the spectrum and revolves around products and services that improve everyday life by elevating spaces and experiences. Originally founded as a value-added steel processor, we expanded our offerings to include manufactured metal products organized around attractive end markets under two separate and distinct reportable operating segments: Building Products and Consumer Products.

We believe the foundation of our success is rooted in our people first philosophy and our belief that people are our most important asset, which serves as a basis for our unwavering commitment to our employees, customers, suppliers, and investors. Our primary goal is to create value for our shareholders. Built on the successful foundation of the Worthington Business System, which encompasses certain proprietary business and management models, procedures, content and materials, we apply a disciplined approach to capital deployment and seek to grow earnings by optimizing our operations and supply chain, developing and commercializing new products and applications, and pursuing strategic investments and acquisitions.

Our fiscal year ends each May 31, and our fiscal quarters end on the final day of each of August, November, February and May. Our common shares are traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "WOR."

On December 1, 2023, we completed the Separation of our former steel processing business into a separate public company in a transaction intended to qualify as tax free to our shareholders, which was accomplished via the Distribution. Worthington Steel is an independent public company. The operating results of our former steel processing business are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented prior to the Separation. All discussions within this Form 10-K, including amounts, percentages and disclosures for all periods presented, reflect only our continuing operations unless otherwise noted.

Following the completion of the Separation, Worthington Industries, Inc. changed its name to Worthington Enterprises, Inc. and its common shares continue trading on the NYSE under the ticker symbol WOR. On December 1, 2023, the common shares of Worthington Steel began trading on the NYSE under the ticker symbol WS.

We believe our established portfolio of market-leading brands positions us well to execute on our growth initiatives and business strategy. Our ability to manufacture at scale and leverage key customer relationships in diverse end markets distinguishes us from our competitors and creates barriers to entry. Our long-standing experience engineering and manufacturing metal and composite products, beginning with our founding as a steel processor in 1955, has given us specialized capabilities in designing and certifying products to meet demanding industry and regulatory standards. We also believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on certain secular trends impacting the markets that we serve, including initiatives that support long-term construction and supply chain investment.

We believe the Worthington Business System is the engine that drives value for our shareholders. The Worthington Business System is rooted in the Worthington Philosophy and designed to drive continuous improvement through use of tools and technologies that help drive results and inform our business decisions by applying lean techniques to streamline costs and reduce waste within manufacturing, commercial, sourcing and supply chain. Through continuous improvement initiatives, we believe we can achieve improved metrics for product quality, service, delivery, workforce safety and waste reduction to further optimize cost, productivity and efficiencies, while creating a resilient and efficient operating platform that can remain agile regardless of external market conditions.

LSI Acquisition: On January 16, 2026, we acquired LSI, one of the largest U.S. manufacturers of standing-seam metal roof clips and retrofit components in the commercial roof market. The purchase price was $206,559, net of cash acquired, including an estimated tax equalization payment of approximately $3,000, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. Refer to "Note P – Acquisitions" for additional information.

Hydrostat Acquisition: On December 3, 2025, we acquired Hydrostat's propane distribution and refurbishment assets. The purchase price was $9,300, net of cash acquired, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. Refer to "Note P – Acquisitions" for additional information.

SES Joint Venture: On October 16, 2025, we divested our 49% interest in the composite business of our SES joint venture. In exchange for our divested interest in the composite business, we received common shares of both Hexagon Composites and Hexagon Purus. The transaction aligns the core remaining capabilities of the SES joint venture – primarily Type 1 low-pressure, steel cylinder and storage infrastructure applications – with our long-term strategic priorities. Refer to "Note C – Investments in Unconsolidated Affiliates" and "Note R – Fair Value Measurements" for additional information.

Elgen Acquisition: On June 18, 2025, we acquired Elgen, a leading provider of HVAC components, ductwork, and structural framing used primarily in commercial building applications across North America. The purchase price was $90,734, net of cash acquired. Refer to "Note P – Acquisitions" for additional information.

Our business is managed and reported under two operating segments that are distinguishable by the nature of the products and services provided: Building Products and Consumer Products. International operations accounted for approximately 12% of consolidated net sales in fiscal 2026, primarily to customers in Europe. Sales to one retail customer accounted for 10% of our consolidated net sales in fiscal 2026.
Refer to the following segment descriptions and "Note O – Segment Data" for a full description of our segments.

Our Building Products business is a market-leading provider of critical components in essential categories, including: (i) pressurized containment solutions for heating, cooking, cooling and water applications; (ii) HVAC systems; (iii) metal roofing clips; and (iv), through our unconsolidated joint ventures, WAVE and ClarkDietrich, ceiling suspension systems and light gauge metal framing products. Product brands within the Building Products portfolio include BPD, CoMet®, Elgen, Logan Stampings, NEXI, PowerCore, Ragasco®, Roof Hugger®, Well-X-Trol® and XLite, among others. Our pressurized containment solutions include refrigerant and LPG cylinders, well water and expansion tanks, and other specialty products which are generally sold to gas producers and distributors. Refrigerant gas cylinders are used to hold refrigerant gases for commercial, residential, and automotive air conditioning and refrigeration systems. LPG cylinders hold fuel for residential and light commercial heating systems, barbeque grills and recreational vehicle equipment, industrial forklifts and commercial/residential cooking (the latter, generally outside North America). Well water tanks and expansion tanks are used primarily in the residential market with certain products also sold to commercial markets. Specialty products include a variety of fire suppression tanks, chemical tanks, and foam and adhesive tanks.

paragraphs: Our future results and the market price for the common shares are subject to numerous risks, many of which are driven by factors that we cannot control or predict. The following discussion, as well as other sections of this Form 10-K, including "Part II – Item 7. – Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," describe certain risks to our business, our results, our strategies and the common shares. Consideration should be given to the risk factors described below as well as those in the "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" section at the beginning of this Form 10-K, in conjunction with reviewing the forward-looking statements and other information contained in this Form 10-K. The risks described below are those that we have identified as material but are not the only risks and uncertainties facing us or our shareholders. Our business is also subject to general risks and uncertainties that affect many other companies, such as market conditions, economic conditions, geopolitical events, changes in laws, rules, regulations or accounting rules, fluctuations in interest rates, terrorism, war or conflicts, major health concerns, natural disasters or other disruptions of expected business conditions. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial also may impair our business, including our results of operations, liquidity and financial condition, and/or the common shares.

Our net sales are heavily concentrated in the consumer products and construction end markets, including residential and non-residential construction, and repair and remodel, and a decline in those end markets may have an adverse impact on our results of operations and cash flows. The consumer products and construction industries account for a significant portion of our net sales, and reduced demand from these industries could adversely affect our business. A downturn in the general economy, a disruption in capital and credit markets, high inflation, high unemployment, reduced consumer confidence or other factors, could cause reductions in demand from our end markets in general and, in particular, the consumer products and construction end markets. If demand for the products we sell to the end markets which we supply were to be reduced, our sales, financial results and cash flows could be negatively affected.

Financial difficulties and bankruptcy filings by our customers could have an adverse impact on our businesses. The financial difficulties of certain customers and/or their failure to obtain credit or otherwise improve their financial condition could result in changes within the markets we serve, including plant closings, decreased production, reduced demand, changes in product mix, unfavorable changes in the prices, terms or conditions we are able to obtain and other changes that may result in decreased purchases from us and otherwise negatively impact our businesses. These conditions also increase the risk that our customers may delay or default on their payment obligations to us. If the general economy or any of our markets decline, the risk of bankruptcy filings by and financial difficulties of our customers may increase. While we have taken and will continue to take steps intended to mitigate the impact of financial difficulties and potential bankruptcy filings by our customers, these matters could have a negative impact on our businesses.

Our operating results may be adversely affected by continued volatility in steel prices. Over the past several years, steel prices have experienced significant volatility driven by supplier consolidation, trade policy developments, and global macroeconomic conditions. More recently, an evolving tariff environment has been a particularly significant driver of domestic steel pricing, as reduced access to competitively priced imported steel has contributed to unpredictable domestic price levels. If steel prices or other raw material prices were to decrease, competitive conditions or contractual obligations may impact how quickly we must reduce our prices to our customers, and we could be forced to use higher-priced raw materials then on hand to complete orders for which the selling prices have decreased. This could result in losses or a write-down of the value of our inventory, and our financial results could be adversely affected.

Our operating results may be affected by fluctuations in raw material prices and our ability to pass on increases in raw material costs to our customers. Our principal raw material is flat-rolled steel, which we purchase from multiple primary steel producers. Our businesses also utilize aluminum, propane, copper and other materials. The steel industry as a whole has been cyclical, and at times availability and pricing can be volatile due to a number of factors beyond our control. These factors include general economic conditions, domestic and worldwide supply and demand, high inflation, the influence of hedge funds and other investment funds participating in commodity markets, curtailed production from major suppliers due to factors such as the closing or idling of facilities, pandemics, international conflicts, accidents or equipment breakdowns, repairs or catastrophic events, labor costs, shortages, strikes or other problems, competition, new laws and regulations, import duties, tariffs, energy costs, availability and cost of steel inputs (e.g., ore, scrap, coal and energy), foreign currency exchange rates and other factors described in the immediately following paragraph. This volatility, as well as any increases in raw material costs, could significantly affect our steel costs and adversely impact our financial results. To manage our exposure to market risk, where possible, we match our customer pricing terms to the pricing terms offered to us by our suppliers in order to minimize the impact of market fluctuations on our margins. However, should our suppliers increase the prices of our critical raw materials, we may not have alternative sources of supply. In addition, in an environment of increasing prices for steel and other raw materials, competitive conditions or contractual obligations may impact how much of the price increases we can pass on to our customers. To the extent we are unable to pass on future price increases in our raw materials to our customers, our financial results could be adversely affected.

The costs of manufacturing our products and our ability to meet our customers' demands could be negatively impacted if we experience interruptions in deliveries of needed raw materials or supplies. If, for any reason, our supply of flat-rolled steel or other key raw materials, such as aluminum, zinc, copper or helium, or other supplies is curtailed or we are otherwise unable to obtain the quantities we need at competitive prices, our business could suffer and our financial results could be adversely affected. Such interruptions could result from a number of factors, including a shortage of capacity in the supplier base of raw materials, energy or the inputs needed to make steel or other supplies, a failure of suppliers to fulfill their supply or delivery obligations, financial difficulties of suppliers resulting in the closing or idling of supplier facilities, other significant events affecting supplier facilities, significant weather events, those factors listed in the immediately preceding paragraph or other factors beyond our control like pandemics. Further, the number of suppliers has decreased in recent years due to industry consolidation and the financial difficulties of certain suppliers, and this consolidation may continue.

Our Building Products business is a market-leading provider of critical components in essential categories, including: (i) pressurized containment solutions for heating, cooking, cooling and water applications; (ii) HVAC systems; (iii) metal roofing clips; and (iv), through our unconsolidated joint ventures, WAVE and ClarkDietrich, ceiling suspension systems and light gauge metal framing products. Activity outside of our two reportable segments is presented within "Other" and "Unallocated Corporate" as described further below.

paragraphs: 於1955年成立，本公司為工具、戶外生活與慶典市場等主要透過零售通路銷售給消費者的產品之領導設計與製造商，並提供廣泛的高專業化建築產品，主要服務住宅與非住宅建設市場之客戶，包括天花板懸吊系統與輕型金屬骨架產品，分別透過未合併之合資企業WAVE與ClarkDietrich，以及本公司擁有與合併之營運業務，生產加壓 containment 解決方案用於加熱、烹飪與冷卻應用，以及其他產品。本公司之業務策略根植於本公司以人為先的文化，重視與各領域之關係，並圍繞著改善日常生活的產品與服務，提升空間與體驗。本公司最初成立為價值增加之鋼鐵加工商，後擴展產品組合，包含製造金屬產品，以吸引人之終端市場為中心，分為兩個獨立且不同的應報告營運分部：建築產品與消費產品。

本公司相信成功之基礎在於本公司以人為先的哲學與本公司相信人為本公司最重要之資產，這為本公司對員工、客戶、供應商與投資者之不渝承諾奠定基礎。本公司之主要目標為為股東創造價值。本公司建立於Worthington商業系統之成功基礎上，該系統包含某些專屬之商業與管理模型、程序、內容與資料，本公司應用嚴謹之方法於資本配置，並追求透過優化營運與供應鏈、開發與商業化新產品與應用，以及追求戰略性投資與併購來成長獲利。
本公司會計年度於每年5月31日結束，會計季節於每年8月、11月、2月與5月之最後一天結束。本公司普通股於紐約證券交易所交易，代號為"WOR."
於2023年12月1日，本公司完成將前鋼鐵加工業務分拆為獨立上市公司之交易，該交易旨在對股東而言為稅務無負擔，此交易透過分發完成。Worthington Steel為一獨立上市公司。本公司前鋼鐵加工業務之營運結果於所有呈報期間均列為已終止營運。本10-K表格內所有討論，包括金額、百分比與揭露資料，均僅反映本公司持續營運，除非另有說明。
於完成分拆後，Worthington Industries, Inc.更名為Worthington Enterprises, Inc.，本公司普通股繼續於紐約證券交易所交易，代號為WOR。於2023年12月1日，Worthington Steel之普通股開始於紐約證券交易所交易，代號為WS。

本公司相信本公司已建立之市場領導品牌組合，使本公司能有效執行成長計畫與業務策略。本公司能於規模製造並運用關鍵客戶關係於多樣終端市場之能力，使本公司與競爭對手有所區別，並創造進入門檻。本公司自1955年成立為鋼鐵加工商以來，長期經驗於工程與製造金屬與複合產品，使本公司具備設計與認證產品以符合嚴格產業與法規標準之專業能力。本公司亦相信本公司處於有利位置，可利用影響本公司服務市場之某些長期趨勢，包括支持長期建設與供應鏈投資之計畫。

本公司相信Worthington商業系統為推動股東價值之引擎。Worthington商業系統根植於Worthington哲學，並設計用以透過使用工具與技術來推動成果並影響本公司商業決策，應用lean技術來簡化成本與減少製造、商業、採購與供應鏈之浪費。透過持續改進計畫，本公司相信可達成產品品質、服務、交貨、工作員安全與浪費減少之改善指標，進一步優化成本、生產力與效率，同時建立一個堅韌且高效的營運平台，即使面對外部市場條件之變動也能保持靈活。
LSI收購：於2026年1月16日，本公司收購LSI，為美國最大的商業屋頂市場之站立式屋頂金屬屋瓦扣件與 retrofit 零組件製造商之一。購併價格為206,559美元，扣除現金取得，包含約3,000美元之稅務平衡支付，並受常規之交割後調整條款約束。有關更多資訊，請參閱"附註P – 收購"。
Hydrostat 收購：於 2025 年 12 月 3 日，本公司取得 Hydrostat 的丙烷配送及翻新資產。買價為 9,300 百萬美元，扣除所收現金後之淨額，並依慣例於交割後進行調整。有關更多資訊，請參閱 "Note P – 收購"。

SES Joint Venture: 2025年10月16日，本公司出售我們在SES合資企業之複合材料業務的49%權益。作為交換，我們收到Hexagon Composites與Hexagon Purus的普通股。此交易使SES合資企業的核心剩餘能力 – 主要是Type 1低壓、鋼氣瓶與儲存基礎設施應用 – 與我們的長期戰略優先事項一致。有關更多資訊，請參閱"Note C – Investments in Unconsolidated Affiliates"和"Note R – Fair Value Measurements"。
Elgen Acquisition: 2025年6月18日，本公司取得Elgen，為北美商業建築應用中主要提供暖通空調零組件、風管與結構骨架的領導供應商。買價為90,734 百萬美元，扣除所取得現金後。有關更多資訊，請參閱"Note P – Acquisitions"。
本公司業務由兩個經營分部管理與報告，其區別在於所提供產品與服務的性質：建築產品與消費性產品。國際業務在財務年度2026年佔合併淨銷售額約12%，主要為歐洲客戶。財務年度2026年，對單一零售客戶的銷售佔本公司合併淨銷售額約10%。
有關分部說明及"Note O – Segment Data"，請參閱以下分部說明。

本公司建築產品業務為市場領先的關鍵零組件供應商，主要產品包括：(i) 用於供暖、烹飪、冷氣與水應用的壓力容器解決方案；(ii) 暖通空調系統；(iii) 金屬屋頂夾具；以及(iv) 透過我們未合併的合資企業WAVE與ClarkDietrich，提供天花板吊架系統與輕質金屬骨架產品。建築產品組閤中的產品品牌包括BPD、CoMet®、Elgen、Logan Stampings、NEXI、PowerCore、Ragasco®、Roof Hugger®、Well-X-Trol®與XLite，以及其他品牌。本公司壓力容器解決方案包括冷媒與LPG氣瓶、井水與擴張水箱，以及其他專業產品，通常銷售給氣體生產商與分銷商。冷媒氣瓶用於商業、住宅與汽車空調與冷凍系統的冷媒氣體儲存。LPG氣瓶用於住宅與輕商業用途的供暖系統、烤肉機與露營車設備、工業叉車與商業/住宅烹飪（後者通常在北美以外地區）。井水水箱與擴張水箱主要用於住宅市場，部分產品也銷售給商業市場。專業產品包括多種滅火水箱、化學水箱與泡沫與黏合劑水箱。

paragraphs: 本公司為創新產品與服務的市場領導設計與製造商，包括製造金屬產品，並以兩個獨立且不同的營運分部，圍繞具吸引力的最終市場進行組織：建築產品與消費性產品。我們的主要目標是為股東創造價值。基於沃丁頓商業系統的成功基礎，我們採用嚴謹的資本運用方式，並透過優化營運與供應鏈、開發與商業化創新產品與應用、以及追求戰略性投資與併購，來成長營收。

我們的建築產品業務為市場領導的關鍵零組件供應商，主要產品包括：(i) 用於加熱、烹飪、冷氣與水應用的壓力容器解決方案；(ii) 空調系統；(iii) 金屬屋頂夾具；以及 (iv) 透過我們未合併的合資公司 WAVE 和 ClarkDietrich，提供天花板懸吊系統與輕量金屬骨架產品。我們的壓力容器解決方案包括冷媒與 LPG 氣瓶、井水與膨脹水箱，以及其他專業產品，這些產品通常銷售給天然氣生產商與經銷商。
我們的消費性產品業務在工具、戶外生活與慶典等類別中擁有多元的產品組合，包括用於火炬與相關配件的丙烷氣瓶、手持火炬、專業手工具與儀器、石膏板工具、丙烷氣瓶露營氣瓶、氦氣填充氣球套組，以及氣體烤盤與披薩烤爐，主要銷售給通路商、零售商與經銷商。
除我們兩個應報告分部之外的活動，則列於 "Other" 與 "Unallocated Corporate" 中，如後文進一步說明。

{'original': 'Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance', 'translated': '法律、法規與合規', 'note': '此為應報告分部'}
paragraphs: 本公司未來的營運成果及普通股的市場價格受到許多風險影響，許多風險是由我們無法控制或預測的因素所驅動。以下討論，以及本表單 10-K 的其他部分，包括「第二部分 – 第七項 – 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」，說明了對本公司業務、營運成果、策略及普通股的某些風險。應考量以下所列風險因素，以及本表單 10-K 開頭的「向前看陳述之警示說明」部分所列的風險因素，並與審閱本表單 10-K 中的向前看陳述及其他資訊一併考量。以下所列的風險是本公司已識別為重要的風險，但並非唯一可能影響本公司或股東的風險與不確定性。本公司業務亦受到影響許多其他公司的普遍風險與不確定性，例如市場條件、經濟條件、地緣政治事件、法律、規則、規範或會計規則的變動、利率波動、恐怖主義、戰爭或衝突、重大健康問題、自然災害或其他預期營運條件的中斷。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或目前認為不重要，也可能影響本公司業務，包括營運成果、流動性與財務狀況，以及普通股。

本公司淨銷售額高度集中於消費性產品與建設業終端市場，包括住宅與非住宅建設，以及修繕與翻新，若這些終端市場出現衰退，可能對本公司營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。消費性產品與建設業佔本公司淨銷售額的相當大比例，若這些產業的買方需求減少，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。整體經濟出現衰退、資本與信貸市場中斷、高通貨膨脹、高失業率、消費者信心下降或其他因素，可能導致本公司終端市場整體需求減少，特別是消費性產品與建設業終端市場的需求減少。若我們所供應終端市場的產品需求減少，可能對本公司銷售額、財務成果與現金流產生負面影響。

我們的客戶遭遇財務困難與破產聲請可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。某些客戶的財務困難及其無法取得信貸或改善財務狀況，可能導致我們所服務的市場出現變化，包括工廠關閉、生產減少、需求下降、產品組合變化、我們所能取得的價格、條款或條件出現不利變化，以及其他可能導致我們銷售減少並對本公司業務產生負面影響的情況。這些情況也增加我們的客戶可能延遲或違約支付我們應收款的風險。若整體經濟或我們所服務的任何市場衰退，我們的客戶聲請破產與財務困難的風險可能增加。雖然我們已採取並會持續採取措施以緩解客戶財務困難與潛在破產聲請的影響，但這些事項可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。

本公司營運成果可能因鋼鐵價格持續波動而受到不利影響。過去幾年，鋼鐵價格經歷了顯著波動，主要由供應商合併、貿易政策發展及全球總體經濟條件所驅動。最近，進口鋼鐵價格的變化環境成為國內鋼鐵價格的重要驅動因素，因減少對具競爭力進口鋼鐵的存取，導致國內價格水平變得難以預測。若鋼鐵價格或其他原材料價格下降，競爭條件或契約義務可能影響我們必須多快降低對客戶的價格，我們可能被迫使用價格較高的現有原材料來完成訂單，而這些訂單的銷售價格已下降。這可能會導致虧損或存貨價值減損，並對本公司財務成果產生不利影響。

本公司營運成果可能因原材料價格波動及我們能否將原材料成本增加轉嫁給客戶而受到影響。我們的主要原材料是平 Rolled 鋼鐵，我們從多個主要鋼鐵生產商處購買。本公司業務也使用鋁、丙烷、銅及其他材料。整體鋼鐵產業具有週期性，有時因許多因素超出我們控制範圍，導致供應與價格出現波動。這些因素包括總體經濟條件、國內與全球供需、高通貨膨脹、影響商品市場的對沖基金及其他投資基金的影響、因如工廠關閉或停工等因素導致主要供應商生產減少、疫情、國際衝突、事故或設備故障、修理或重大事件、勞動成本、短缺、罷工或其他問題、競爭、新法律與規範、進口稅、關稅、能源成本、鋼鐵投入物資（如礦石、廢鋼、煤與能源）的可得性與成本、外匯匯率及其他因素，如後述段落所列。這種波動以及任何原材料成本增加，可能顯著影響我們的鋼鐵成本，並對財務成果產生不利影響。為管理市場風險，我們在可能的情況下，將客戶的價格條款與我們從供應商處獲得的價格條款匹配，以減少市場波動對我們毛利率的影響。然而，若我們的供應商提高我們關鍵原材料的價格，我們可能沒有替代的供應來源。此外，在鋼鐵及其他原材料價格持續上升的環境中，競爭條件或契約義務可能影響我們能轉嫁給客戶的價格增加幅度。若我們無法將未來原材料價格增加轉嫁給客戶，可能對財務成果產生不利影響。

若我們遭遇所需原材料或供應品的供應中斷，可能影響我們製造產品的成本及滿足客戶需求的能力。若因任何原因，我們無法取得平 Rolled 鋼鐵或其他關鍵原材料，如鋁、鋅、銅或氦氣，或其他供應品，或無法以具競爭力的價格取得所需數量，可能導致業務受損，並對財務成果產生不利影響。這種中斷可能來自多種因素，包括原材料供應商基礎的容量不足、能源或製造鋼鐵或其他供應品所需投入物資的短缺、供應商未能履行供應或交貨義務、供應商財務困難導致工廠關閉或停工、影響供應商工廠的其他重大事件、重大天氣事件、前一段落所列因素，或其他我們無法控制的因素如疫情。此外，近年來供應商數量因產業合併及部分供應商財務困難而減少，這種合併可能持續進行。
